implementation_notes: Scala's characteristic god object is implicit: an `implicit val appCtx: AppContext` in scope resolves the god object at every call site, so no signature ever mentions it and the coupling is invisible to the compiler's reader. The cure is to make the dependency explicit again — pass `AppContext` (or its parts) as an ordinary parameter and keep implicits for what they are for (typeclasses, summoning), not for state. The other Scala route is the domain `case class` that accumulates fields until it is a record of the entire aggregate's state plus its invariants plus its I/O; splitting means one case class per invariant plus a function per transition.
idiom_name: implicitly summoned Context object; case class holding the world
pitfalls: `implicitly[Payments]` in a signature documents the dependency but restores god-ness if the summon is of the app-wide context.
`case class` copy() calls let any caller rewrite the entire state vector, which is how a value type becomes the system's god object.
Spray/json or circe codecs generated for a god case class break on every schema change, so the god object silently becomes an API contract.
